Windows of Heaven
Windows of Heaven

points: Elisha declares the word of the Most High that within a day the famine will break and fine flour and barley will sell cheaply in the gate of Samaria.

note.label: 2 Kings 7: The Word of the Lord in the Gate of Samaria

points: The lord on whose hand the king leaned doubts the word, asking if the Most High would make windows in heaven. Elisha tells him he will see it with his eyes but not eat of it.

note.label: 2 Kings 7: The Word of the Lord in the Gate of Samaria

points: Four leprous men at the gate reason that they will die either way, so they go over to the camp of the Syrians hoping to be spared.

note.label: 2 Kings 7: The Word of the Lord in the Gate of Samaria

points: The Most High had made the host of the Syrians hear the noise of chariots and horses, so they fled in the twilight and left everything behind.

note.label: 2 Kings 7: The Word of the Lord in the Gate of Samaria

points: The lepers eat and drink and carry off silver, gold, and raiment, hiding the spoil for themselves.

note.label: 2 Kings 7: The Word of the Lord in the Gate of Samaria

points: The lepers realize this is a day of good tidings and that they should not hold their peace, so they report to the king's household.

note.label: 2 Kings 7: The Word of the Lord in the Gate of Samaria

points: The king suspects a trap, thinking the Syrians are hiding in the field to catch Israel coming out of the city.

note.label: 2 Kings 7: The Word of the Lord in the Gate of Samaria

points: Messengers sent to investigate find the way to Jordan full of garments and vessels cast away in the Syrians' haste, and the people go out and spoil the tents, so the food is sold cheaply exactly as the word said.

note.label: 2 Kings 7: The Word of the Lord in the Gate of Samaria

points: The king sets the doubting lord in charge of the gate, and the people trod upon him there and he died, just as the man of God had spoken.
The trampling in the gate stands as a picture of a crowd stampeding after goods, hating one another over things, and here it became the judgment on a man who doubted the word.

note.label: 2 Kings 7: The Word of the Lord in the Gate of Samaria

points: The lord saw the plenty with his eyes but did not eat of it, so the word of the Most High fell out to the letter.
